Anton Chekhov, Uncle Vanya, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anton-chekhov/uncle-vanya/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Anton Chekhov, the author, died 1904 (Wikidata Q5685, P570 1904-07-02 and 1904-07-15).
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946 (Wikidata Q2495818, P570 1946-12-17).

First publication of the text used: 1923, the English translation by Constance Garnett. The Russian play was published in 1897. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Uncle Vanya was published in 1897 by Anton Chekhov. It was translated from Russian in 1923 by Constance Garnett.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1923 and the original in 1897, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: Russian work by Anton Chekhov (died 1904), first published 1897. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator Constance Garnett (died 1946) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2017, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anton-chekhov/uncle-vanya/constance-garnett): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q5685 (Anton Chekhov), P570 1904-07-02 and 1904-07-15.
